disclaimer: General fitness and nutrition education, not medical advice. If you have a medical condition, check with a doctor (e.g. University of Ghana Hospital, Legon) before starting.
values_note: Food protein/kcal values are rounded approximations for typical Ghanaian portions (FAO/INFOODS West African Food Composition Table 2019; USDA FoodData Central). Display with '~'.

fields.label: Daily activity outside the gym
fields.hint: If unsure between two, pick the lower one.

onboarding.storage: device_only; weight, waist and photos excluded from any sync/analytics by default

activity_descriptions.sedentary: Mostly sitting (lectures, laptop), little walking, no training
activity_descriptions.moderately_active: On your feet a lot, or train 4-5x/week, or 10k+ steps daily
activity_descriptions.extra_active: Athlete training twice a day or heavy manual labour

tdee.note: Includes training; do not add exercise calories on top.

reference_weight.rule: if bmi < 25: weight_kg; elif goal_weight_kg: max(goal_weight_kg, ref_bmi*height_m^2); else ref_bmi*height_m^2

protein.rationale: ISSN 1.4-2.0 g/kg (higher in a deficit); Morton 2018 plateau ~1.6 g/kg (CI to 2.2). For BMI>=25 scale to reference (BMI-25 or goal) weight, since adipose tissue has minimal protein requirement; avoids impractical 200 g+ targets.

items.label: 1 palm (~100 g) chicken / goat / beef / fish
250 ml milk or 3 tbsp milk powder

good_day_rule: protein >= good_day_points AND >= 3 of the other 5 items

portion_guide.swallow_rule: Start at 3/4 of your usual kenkey/banku/fufu ball or waakye scoop; after 2 weeks try 1/2 if hunger is fine. Keep the fish/meat portion.

meal_ideas.name: Oats + milk + eggs
components: 250 ml milk or 3 tbsp milk powder
meal_ideas.tips: Little or no sugar; sweeten with banana.

meal_ideas.name: Hausa koko upgrade
meal_ideas.tips: Plain koko is ~3 g protein; milk + eggs make it a meal. Max 3 koose (fried).

meal_ideas.name: Egg bread
meal_ideas.tips: Ask for less margarine/oil. Add a 4th egg for +6 g.

meal_ideas.name: Tuna with gari foto or yam
components: 1 cupped hand gari foto or boiled yam
meal_ideas.tips: Tuna in brine is leaner than in oil.

meal_ideas.name: Red red, upgraded
meal_ideas.tips: Ask for less palm oil and fewer fried plantain slices.

meal_ideas.name: Waakye, smart order
meal_ideas.tips: Skip/limit gari, spaghetti (talia), extra shito. A full 'everything' plate is often 1,100+ kcal. Wele adds little useful protein.

meal_ideas.name: Kenkey with fish
components: 1 medium fried/grilled fish or 4-5 keta school boys
meal_ideas.tips: Kenkey is mostly carbs (~8-10 g protein per ball). Get 2 fish rather than 2 balls; grilled over fried.

meal_ideas.name: Banku and tilapia
meal_ideas.tips: Lean, high-protein. Share a big banku.

meal_ideas.name: Light soup with fish or goat
meal_ideas.tips: Low-oil soup. The meat pieces are what count.

meal_ideas.name: Groundnut soup, smart
meal_ideas.tips: Calorie-dense: skim the oil layer, keep the ball small.

meal_ideas.name: Kontomire stew + ampesi
components: kontomire stew with 2 eggs or momone/mackerel
meal_ideas.tips: 1 tbsp palm oil per serving at home.

meal_ideas.name: Garden egg stew + yam
components: garden egg stew with tinned mackerel or 2 eggs

meal_ideas.name: Jollof / fried rice + chicken
meal_ideas.tips: Ask for grilled chicken, less rice and less coleslaw dressing.

meal_ideas.name: Khebab snack
meal_ideas.tips: Great post-gym snack; skip the fried yam.

meal_ideas.name: Soya chunks stew
components: 40 g dry soya chunks in stew

meal_ideas.name: Yoghurt + groundnuts
meal_ideas.tips: Pick plain/low-sugar over sweet sachet drinks.

meal_ideas.name: Milk drink
components: ~40 g milk powder in water or 500 ml fresh milk

meal_ideas.name: Indomie + 2 eggs + veg
meal_ideas.tips: Noodles alone are low protein; always add eggs and veg; use half the seasoning oil.

protocol: Same scale on hard flat floor
weigh_in.message: Your weight bounces day to day. Only the weekly average matters.

waist.protocol: Standing relaxed, end of normal exhale, 2 readings averaged

weekly_check_in.rate_expression: (avg_this_week - avg_last_week)/avg_last_week*100  (negative = loss); use 2-week mean once >=3 weeks of data

rules.message: Losing a bit fast. Add one protein snack (~150 kcal) to protect muscle and energy.
Slow but steady. If your waist isn't dropping, add 1,000 steps.
Plateau. First check protein points, portions and drinks. If those are solid, we'll trim 150 kcal or add 2,000 steps.

rules.condition: abs(loss_pct) < 0.25 AND waist decreasing AND strength increasing
rules.message: The scale is lying: waist down and strength up means you're losing fat and gaining muscle.
Weight is creeping up. Review portions and drinks first.

rules.condition: user reports exhaustion/poor sleep AND strength dropping
rules.message: You may be under-fuelled or stressed. Eat a bit more and prioritise sleep.

expectations_timeline.strength: Learning machines and form; soreness; weights feel awkward, that's normal.
Fast neural gains, often +10-20% on machines; soreness fades.

expectations_timeline.scale_kg: -0.4 to -0.7 per week; some flat weeks are normal
expectations_timeline.body: Clothes looser; waist -3 to -6 cm total
Visible in photos; waist -5 to -8 cm total
expectations_timeline.strength: Many lifts +30-50% vs week 1; first plateaus on some lifts.

expectations_timeline.body: ~1-2 kg muscle gain likely, hidden by fat loss

adherence.habit_badge_rule: 4 of 5 days per week for a habit row
adherence.implementation_intention_template: After my [cue, e.g. last lecture on Mon/Wed/Fri], I will [walk to the gym].

parq.source: Paraphrased from PAR-Q+ (Warburton et al.; 2023 form at eparmedx.com). Link to the official form.

on_any_yes.message: Please talk to a doctor (e.g. University of Ghana Hospital, Legon) before starting, or complete the full PAR-Q+ follow-up. You can still browse the app.
on_any_yes.ack_label: I've been cleared by a doctor to exercise

questions.text: Has a doctor ever told you that you have a heart condition or high blood pressure?
Do you feel pain in your chest at rest, during daily activities, or when you are physically active?
In the past 12 months, have you lost balance because of dizziness or lost consciousness?
questions.note: Answer NO if dizziness came only from hard breathing during vigorous exercise.

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with another chronic medical condition (e.g. diabetes, asthma, kidney disease, sickle cell disease)?
Are you currently taking prescribed medicine for a chronic medical condition?
Do you currently have, or have you had in the past 12 months, a bone, joint or soft-tissue (muscle, ligament, tendon) problem that could get worse with more activity?
questions.note: Answer NO if it no longer limits you.

questions.text: Has a doctor ever said you should only do medically supervised physical activity?

ghana_extra_questions.text: Do you have sickle cell trait (AS) or sickle cell disease (SS/SC)?

advice.trait: Hydrate well, avoid all-out efforts in heat, build intensity gradually over 3-4 weeks, stop at unusual muscle pain or breathlessness.
advice.disease: Please get a doctor's clearance first.

ghana_extra_questions.text: Have you had malaria, typhoid or a fever in the past 2 weeks?
ghana_extra_questions.advice: Wait until 1-2 weeks after full recovery, then restart at 50% of usual loads.

ghana_extra_questions.text: Do you have diabetes or take blood-sugar medicines?
ghana_extra_questions.advice: Carry a sweet snack and don't train fasted.

red_flags_stop_now: Chest pain, pressure or tightness, or pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
Severe breathlessness out of proportion to effort, or wheeze that won't settle
Fainting, near-fainting, sudden dizziness or confusion
Sudden severe headache, vision change, or weakness/numbness on one side
Sharp joint pain, a 'pop' with pain or swelling, or pain that changes how you move
After a session: dark/cola-coloured urine with severe muscle pain or swelling (possible rhabdomyolysis) - go to hospital the same day

heat_illness.action: Pause, drink water/ORS, move to shade or a fan.
Stop training. Cool place, lie down legs up, sip water/ORS, loosen clothing. Get help if not better in 30 min.
Call 112 / 193. Cool aggressively right away (cold water/ice on body, fanning) while waiting.

heat_prevention: Train in cooler parts of the day when possible.
Drink 400-600 ml in the 2 hours before training.
Rest longer between sets if the gym is hot.
Heat acclimatisation takes ~10-14 days, so go easier in your first 2 weeks.
Be extra careful after illness, poor sleep or alcohol.

milestone_notes: No milestone depends on the ambiguous 'ankle machine'. Machine loads use an editable per-machine sled/carriage weight. Body milestones use 7-day averages only.

rest_timer_tips: Sip water now, a few mouthfuls every rest.
Breathe slowly through your nose; you're ready when you can talk in full sentences.
Next set: same weight. If all reps felt easy (2+ left in the tank), add a small step next time.
Shake out your arms and legs, but stay near your station.
Wipe the bench/seat before you leave the machine.
Check your setup for the next set: seat height, grip, feet flat.
Stopping 1-3 reps before failure is ideal for beginners.
Hot in here? It's fine to rest 30 extra seconds.
Quality reps beat heavy, sloppy reps.
Write down how hard that felt (easy / just right / hard); the app uses it to progress you.
pre_workout: Eat a meal with carbs + protein 1-3 hours before (e.g. egg bread, red red, kenkey + fish), not a heavy oily plate right before.
Drink 400-600 ml of water in the 2 hours before training.
Pack: towel, 1-1.5 L bottle, charged phone, earphones.
Short on time? Do the 20-minute version. Showing up is the win.
Training soon after a long fast? A banana or small koko 30-60 min before helps.
Skip energy drinks; if you like coffee, a small cup is enough.
warm_up: 5 minutes on the bike or treadmill until you're lightly sweating.
Do 1-2 light warm-up sets of your first exercise before working sets.
In Accra's heat you warm up fast, so don't overdo the cardio warm-up.
during_workout_heat: Aim for a few mouthfuls of water every rest; about 500-750 ml across the session.
Feeling dizzy, nauseous or cold and clammy? Stop and cool down; it may be heat exhaustion.
Confusion or collapse in someone is an emergency: call 112 / 193 and cool them with water.
post_workout: Get 25-40 g protein within a couple of hours (e.g. 3 khebab sticks, sardine bread, 4 boiled eggs, tilapia).
Refill your water: drink until your urine is pale again.
Sweated a lot? Salt your food normally or take ORS.
A short 10-minute walk later helps soreness.
Log how you felt; it shapes your next session.
daily_nutrition: Protein at every meal: about 2 palms.
Shrink the swallow, keep the fish.
Ask for grilled over fried, and small shito.
Skim the oil layer off groundnut and palm-nut soups.
Swap the soft drink or malt for water; that's ~200-250 kcal saved.
Add kontomire, garden eggs, okro, cabbage or fruit to 2+ meals.
Spend the extra cedi on an extra egg or fish, not extra gari or talia.
hydration: Your water target is shown in 500 ml sachets.
Pale-straw urine means you're hydrated; dark yellow means drink more.
Don't force more than ~1 L per hour; over-drinking plain water can be dangerous.
Harmattan dryness still dehydrates you; keep drinking.
sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours; muscle is built while you recover.
Same wake time every day, even weekends.
No big coffee or energy drinks after 3 pm.
Exam all-nighter? Make tomorrow's session the 20-minute version.
soreness: Soreness 1-3 days after training is normal in your first weeks; it fades by week 3.
Easy walking and moving help more than total rest.
Sharp or joint pain, swelling, or soreness worsening after 3 days is not normal; rest and get it checked.
Dark/cola urine with severe muscle pain: go to hospital the same day.
missed_session: Missed one? No problem. Just don't miss twice.
Your streak is weekly; you can still make this week count.
Ill with fever or malaria? Use pause mode and come back 1-2 weeks after recovery.
Do the next session in your plan; no need to 'make up' the missed one.
plateau: Weight flat but waist down? That's recomposition, so keep going.
Check the basics first: protein points, portion sizes, sugary drinks.
We change one thing at a time: -150 kcal or +2,000 steps.
Plateaus of 1-2 weeks are normal; we look at 3-week trends.
weigh_in: Weigh in the morning, after the toilet, before eating or drinking.
Big kenkey/banku night or salty soup? Expect a temporary jump tomorrow.
gym_etiquette: Busy gym? Offer to share a machine (alternate sets).
Ask a gym staff member to show you a machine if unsure; everyone was a beginner.
budget: Eggs by the crate and beans in bulk are the cheapest protein.
Keep 3-4 tins of sardines/mackerel in your room.
Milk powder turns koko, oats and gari into protein.
Abobi or shrimp powder: +5-10 g protein for pesewas.
Creatine monohydrate (3-5 g/day) is the only supplement worth it if money allows; skip fat burners.
safety: Stop immediately for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness or palpitations.
Emergency: 112, Ambulance: 193. Nearest: University of Ghana Hospital, Legon.
Sickle cell trait? Hydrate well and build intensity gradually.
